title: WPMS/2734/2015 of Ganesh Chandra Joshi Vs Nainital Lake Special Area Development Authority AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Review Application No. 790 of 2015
Interim Relief Applications No. 12627 & 13348 of 2015
Misc. Application Nos. 2816/2016; 15034 & 16121 of 2018
In
Writ Petition No. 2734 (MS) of 2015
Ganesh Chandra Joshi. ÖÖ....Petitioner.
Versus
Nainital Lake Special Area Development
and another. ÖÖ Respondents.
Present:
Mr. T.A. Khan, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Aditya Arya, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the respondents.
Mr. M.C. Kandpal, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Chitrarath Kandpal, Advocate for the review
applicant.
Honíble Alok Singh, J.
1. The facts of the present case are that petitioner and review
applicant are brothers. Their father namely Sri Ramesh Chandra
Joshi died on 02.06.2010. During his lifetime, Sri Ramesh Chandra
Joshi divided his properties between the family members
including petitioner and review applicant vide settlement dated
01.11.2000 copy whereof is Annexure No. 4 to the writ petition.
On 03.04.2007, Sri Ramesh Chandra Joshi (father) and petitioner
entered into an agreement with one Sri Sayyad Farad Shah and
according to which, Sri Sayyad Farad Shah would construct a
hotel on the land of petitioner and do tourism business thereon
and would pay Rs. 60,000/- per annum to Sri Ramesh Chandra
Joshi. On 19.02.2008, respondent no. 1 issued notice to the
petitioner and Mr. Sayyad Farad Shah for demolition of said
hotel. Petitioner filed an affidavit and application before
respondent no. 1 that he had not entered into agreement with Mr.
Sayyad Farad Shah, therefore, construction may be demolished.
Thereafter, vide order dated 03.12.2008 respondent no. 1 passed
an order for demolition and consequential order for sealing was

2
passed by respondent no. 2 on 08.06.2015 whereagainst petitioner
filed appeal before Commissioner, Kumaon Mandal, Nainital.
This appeal was dismissed by the Commissioner vide order dated
21.10.2015. Feeling aggrieved, petitioner has approached this
Court by way of filing present writ petition. In the meantime,
mother of petitioner namely Smt. Meera Devi filed a partition suit
before Assistant Collector 1st Class Nainital registered as Revenue
Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11, which is still pending. Copy of the
plaint is Annexure No. 8 the review application. Present writ
petition was disposed on 04.11.2015 by giving following direction:
 ìi. The petitioner shall move an application for
compounding before the respondent authority within
a week. The respondent authority shall pass reasoned
and speaking order on the same within two weeksí
thereafter. Needless to say, that if the construction is
compoundable one, the petitioner shall pay
compounding fee, as per rules.
 ii) If certain portion of the hotel is found to be non-compoundable, the petitioner shall demolish the same
within next three weeks on its own, failing which the
respondent authority shall be at liberty to proceed
against the petitioner, in accordance with law.
 iii) The premises in question shall be de-sealed in the
meanwhile.
 iv) If clause (ii) of this order is not complied with by
the petitioner, the respondent authority shall be at
liberty to seal it again.î
2. Mr. M. C. Kandpal, learned Sr. Advocate for the review
applicant submits that petitioner and review applicant are

3
brothers and co-sharers in the property, in question; area of the
property has not been demarcated yet, as the partition suit filed
by their mother is still pending before the Assistant Collector;
petitioner wants to grab this land by showing himself to be the
owner of the said land, therefore, in order to buttress his claim, he
had filed present writ petition without making the review
applicant as party.
3. Conduct of the petitioner is dubious. On the one hand, he
had moved application and affidavit before respondent no. 1 that
construction may be demolished while on the other, he has filed
present writ petition challenging the consequential order passed
by respondent no. 2. Right of the parties over the land is yet to be
decided, as partition suit is still pending. Therefore, considering
the facts and circumstances of the case, review application is
allowed. Order dated 04.11.2015 passed by this Court is recalled.
Writ petition stands disposed of by directing the Assistant
Collector, 1st Class, Nainital to decide Revenue Case No. 27/2 of
2010-11 at the earliest preferably within six months, after giving
opportunity of hearing to each party. Till the decision is taken by
the Assistant Collector in the said case, parties shall maintain
status quo and orders dated 21.10.2015 and 08.06.2015 passed by
Commissioner and respondent no. 2 respectively shall be kept in
abeyance.
